nodes.content: Develop offline policy improvement certificates that remain valid under bounded hidden confounding without requiring full action coverage.
requirements: Certificates attain at least 95% coverage of true policy gains under the stated confounding bound.
Certify strictly positive gains over the behavior policy in a nontrivial, explicitly characterized regime.

nodes.content: Use sample-split Γ-odds sensitivity bounds to certify supported-action policy switches when their 95% lower gain bound exceeds zero.
What overlap and reward-gap conditions yield positive Γ-robust lower gain bounds for supported-action switches?
In eight-stratum binary bandits with unit-bounded rewards, Γ≤1.25, switched-action propensity≥0.2, switch-mass≥0.1, and observed gap≥0.3 yield positive 95% bounds at n≥20,000.
Simulate 10,000 confounded eight-stratum bandits (n=20,000, Γ=1.25, propensity≥0.2, switch-mass≥0.1, gap≥0.3); measure true-gain coverage and positive-certification frequency.
Across 10,000 eight-stratum bandits meeting the hypothesized thresholds (n=20,000), true-gain coverage was 95.4%; every lower bound was positive.
Audit 2,000 boundary bandits (n=20,000; Γ=1.25; gap=0.3; switch-mass=0.1) with unsupported unswitched actions; measure coverage and certification.
Among 2,000 boundary bandits (switched-action propensity=0.20, gap=0.30, switch-mass=0.10), 11% had nonpositive bounds; true-gain coverage was 95.2%.
Raising the observed gap threshold to 0.40 should yield ≥95% positive certificates while maintaining ≥95% true-gain coverage.
Rerun 2,000 boundary bandits with gap≥0.40, propensity≥0.2, switch-mass≥0.1, n=20,000, Γ=1.25; measure positive-certification rate and true-gain coverage.
In 2,000 boundary bandits with gap≥0.40, positive-certification rate reached 97.1% and true-gain coverage reached 95.3%.
Stress-test 5,000 Γ=1.25 adversarially confounded bandits with unsupported unswitched actions and gap≥0.40; measure positive-certification rate and true-gain coverage.
Across 5,000 adversarial bandits (n=20,000, Γ=1.25, switched-action propensity≥0.2, switch-mass≥0.1, gap≥0.40), positive-certification was 91.8%; true-gain coverage was 95.2%.
With n≥20,000, propensity≥0.2, switch-mass≥0.1, and Γ-adjusted gap≥0.20, predict ≥95% positive certification and coverage under adversarial Γ=1.25.
Derive Γ-robust switched-stratum gain bounds with simultaneous 95% confidence correction, then stress-test the Γ-adjusted gap≥0.20 regime.
Simulate 5,000 adversarial Γ=1.25 bandits (n=20,000; propensity≥0.2; switch-mass≥0.1; adjusted gap≥0.20) with unsupported unswitched actions; measure certification and coverage.
Among 5,000 adversarial bandits with Γ-adjusted gap≥0.20, positive certification reached 96.4% and true-gain coverage reached 95.3%.
AdversarialBandit-5K contains 5,000 seeded Γ=1.25 simulations, unsupported-action masks, certificate bounds, and true-gain coverage records.
Adopt Γ-adjusted gap≥0.20: raw gap≥0.40 certified 97.1% in boundary cases but 91.8% adversarially, versus 96.4% with ≥95% coverage.
Use negative-control proxy bridges and Γ-robust 95% bounds to certify supported switches without evaluating unchanged unsupported actions.
Fit proxy bridges in 5,000 simulated eight-stratum bandits (Γ=1.25, n=20,000) with unsupported unswitched actions; measure true-gain coverage and positive certification.
Across 5,000 Γ=1.25 bandits with valid negative controls and adjusted gap≥0.20, proxy-bridge bounds achieved 95.5% coverage and 97.0% positive certification.
ProxyBridge-5K includes seeded eight-stratum bandits, valid negative-control proxies, fitted bridges, unsupported-action masks, and 95% gain certificates.
Adopt proxy bridges only with defensible negative controls: simulated coverage reached 95.5% and positive certification reached 97.0%.
Intersect 97.5% gain intervals from randomized audit and Γ-confounded logs on supported switches to obtain 95% certificates.
How many randomized audit samples per switched stratum make intersected 95% gain bounds positive at Γ=1.25?
At Γ=1.25, 800 audit samples per switched stratum (400 per action) yield ≥95% positive certificates for true gaps≥0.25.
Test intersected 97.5% intervals across 5,000 Γ=1.25 bandits with 800 audits/switched stratum and true gap≥0.25; measure coverage and certification.
Across 5,000 Γ=1.25 bandits, intersected bounds with 800 audits/switched stratum achieved 95.4% true-gain coverage and 96.2% positive certification.
In the 1,000 eight-switch subset, uncorrected stratumwise intersections covered total gain only 92.8%, below the promised 95%.
Reject uncorrected stratumwise intersections despite 96.2% positive certification; require simultaneous correction because eight-switch gain coverage fell to 92.8%.
Certify total switched-stratum gain directly using Γ-robust aggregate bounds and a single 95% confidence interval, avoiding stratumwise intersections.
Derive one 95% Γ-robust aggregate bound for supported switches; test coverage and positive certification on ProxyBridge-5K at adjusted gap≥0.20.
On ProxyBridge-5K, compute single 95% Γ=1.25 aggregate switched-gain bounds for adjusted gaps≥0.20; measure true-gain coverage and positive certification.
On ProxyBridge-5K, aggregate Γ=1.25 bounds covered true policy gain in 95.6% of runs and certified positive gain in 96.1%.
On ProxyBridge-5K eight-switch cases, test aggregate Γ=1.25 bounds for gain coverage and positive certification with unsupported unswitched actions.
In 1,000 ProxyBridge-5K eight-switch cases, aggregate bounds covered true gain only 93.6%, despite 96.0% positive certification.
EightSwitchAudit-v1 contains 1,000 ProxyBridge-5K eight-switch cases, aggregate bounds, true gains, and the 93.6% coverage diagnostic.
Reject uncorrected aggregate bounds: overall coverage was 95.6%, but eight-switch coverage fell to 93.6%, violating the 95% target.
Use sample-split Γ-robust switch bounds with simultaneous Bonferroni-Hoeffding radii, certifying positive gains without evaluating unchanged unsupported actions.
Does simultaneous Bonferroni-Hoeffding correction retain positive certificates for eight switches at n=20,000 and Γ-adjusted gap≥0.20?
For eight switches at n=20,000 and adjusted gaps≥0.20, simultaneous bounds achieve ≥95% true-gain coverage and ≥80% positive certification.
Recompute simultaneous Bonferroni-Hoeffding bounds on EightSwitchAudit-v1 (n=20,000, Γ=1.25, adjusted gap≥0.20); estimate coverage and positive-certification rates.
On 1,000 EightSwitchAudit-v1 cases, simultaneous bounds covered true gain in 96.1% but certified positive gain in only 73.4%.
At n=20,000, raising eight-switch Γ-adjusted gaps to ≥0.30 yields ≥80% positive certificates and ≥95% true-gain coverage.
Filter EightSwitchAudit-v1 for eight-switch cases with Γ-adjusted gaps≥0.30; recompute simultaneous bounds and measure coverage and positive-certification rate.
Among 500 EightSwitchAudit-v1 cases with Γ-adjusted gaps≥0.30, simultaneous bounds achieved 96.0% true-gain coverage and 84.2% positive certification.
EightSwitchAudit-v2 adds simultaneous Bonferroni-Hoeffding gain bounds and adjusted-gap≥0.30 flags for 500 qualifying cases.
Retain simultaneous bounds with eight-switch adjusted gap≥0.30: certification rose from 73.4% to 84.2%, with 96.0% coverage.
Use Γ-adjusted sensitivity bounds (gap≥0.20), validated proxies when available, and simultaneous correction for eight switches (gap≥0.30); reject uncorrected alternatives.
